shortDescription: West African crude oil differentials were little changed on Friday, though an uptick in Chinese buying could be providing a floor to differentials, traders said.

children: West African crude oil differentials were little changed on Friday, though an uptick in Chinese buying could be providing a floor to differentials, traders said.

Chinese demand was helping to slow the slide in West African differentials, two traders said, after mounting pressure in recent weeks from record-high freight rates. West African grades tend to travel long-haul to their main demand outlets
However, the overhang of November cargoes will have to clear before pressure in the West African crude market can really let up, one of the traders added
November cargoes are waiting to clear while December loading schedules are already out
Exports of four key Nigerian crude oil grades are expected to increase. They are estimated to average 888,000 bpd in December versus 874,000 bpd in November, preliminary programmes showed
There were no bids or offers for West African crudes in the Platts window on Friday, another trader said

In downstream news, Cameroon's state oil refiner Sonara said on Friday that it had signed an agreement with Nigeria's Dangote Group and Lagos-based MRS Oil & Gas Company to supply refined petroleum products to Cameroon
